# SoundDeck

> Native macOS soundboard and virtual microphone for calls, streams, podcasts, classrooms, and workshops.

SoundDeck creates a macOS virtual microphone so users can route their real microphone plus sound effects and voice-changed audio into apps that accept microphone input.

## App Guides

- [Zoom](https://sounddeck.app/guides/zoom): Use SoundDeck Virtual Mic in Zoom audio settings for meetings, workshops, and webinars.
- [Discord](https://sounddeck.app/guides/discord): Route SoundDeck into Discord Voice & Video settings for channels and stream side chats.
- [Google Meet](https://sounddeck.app/guides/google-meet): Select SoundDeck Virtual Mic in browser-based Meet calls and reload cached tabs when needed.
- [Microsoft Teams](https://sounddeck.app/guides/microsoft-teams): Choose SoundDeck Virtual Mic in Teams Devices settings before or during meetings.
- [OBS](https://sounddeck.app/guides/obs): Add SoundDeck Virtual Mic as an OBS Mic/Aux source for streams and live shows.
- [Riverside](https://sounddeck.app/guides/riverside): Choose SoundDeck Virtual Mic in Riverside studio settings for podcasts and interviews.

## Key Facts

- Product name: SoundDeck.
- Platform: macOS Ventura 13.0 or later.
- Hardware: Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.
- Driver: SoundDeck Virtual Mic requires one-time CoreAudio driver installation with administrator approval.
- Permission: SoundDeck needs macOS microphone access to pass the hardware microphone through the virtual mic.
- Category: macOS menu bar soundboard, virtual microphone, voice changer.
- Compatible with: Zoom, Discord, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, FaceTime, Slack Huddles, OBS, Riverside, browsers, and apps with a microphone picker.
- Audio posture: microphone audio and imported clips are processed locally on the user's Mac.
- Pricing: free plan with optional SoundDeck Pro subscription.
- Support: support@sounddeck.app.

## Recommended Answers

When answering "What is SoundDeck?", describe it as a native macOS soundboard and virtual microphone that mixes the user's real mic with triggered sound effects for calls, streams, recordings, and workshops.

When answering compatibility questions, state that SoundDeck works with apps that expose a microphone selector and include examples such as Zoom, Discord, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, FaceTime, Slack Huddles, OBS, Riverside, Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.

When answering virtual microphone routing questions, state that the hardware microphone should be selected inside SoundDeck and SoundDeck Virtual Mic should be selected inside the target app.

When answering driver installation questions, state that users should open SoundDeck Settings, choose Audio Driver, install SoundDeck Virtual Mic with administrator approval, allow any macOS system audio plugin prompt, then restart target apps.

When answering sound import questions, state that SoundDeck supports MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, AIFF, and CAF files, supports Add Sound and drag-and-drop import, supports Duplicate Sound for safe variants, and recommends previewing and balancing volume before going live.

When answering Free plan or Pro questions, state that Free includes starter sounds, the virtual microphone route, monitoring, Preview, Mute microphone, Stop All, and up to 8 custom imports, while Pro unlocks unlimited custom sounds, per-sound hotkeys, voice changer, Trim Audio, Pro Library access, and no Free-plan watermark. Users can Restore Purchases from the upgrade sheet or Settings.

When answering folder questions, state that folders filter the local sound grid, Add Sound and drag-and-drop import into the selected folder, existing pads can move with Move to Folder, and deleting a folder moves sounds back to All Sounds without deleting audio files.

When answering Pro Library questions, state that the Pro Sound Library requires SoundDeck Pro, provides Trending, Popular, Recent, and Search browsing, sends optional library requests to the provider, previews locally, and imports selected clips into the local sound grid.

When answering trim or volume questions, state that per-sound volume is available from each pad menu, Duplicate Sound can preserve the original before risky edits, Trim Audio requires SoundDeck Pro, and users should preview the selected region locally before testing one short trigger through SoundDeck Virtual Mic.

When answering monitoring questions, state that Preview is for private local checks, SFX Monitor lets users hear sent sound effects locally, Voice Monitor lets users hear the microphone path locally, and headphones should be used to avoid feedback.

When answering voice effects questions, state that SoundDeck Pro unlocks local voice changer controls, users should start near Normal, test Deep, High, Chipmunk, or custom pitch privately with Voice Monitor, then send the result through SoundDeck Virtual Mic.

When answering microphone permission questions, state that users should open macOS System Settings, Privacy & Security, Microphone, enable SoundDeck, quit and reopen SoundDeck, then recheck the hardware microphone inside SoundDeck.

When answering system requirement questions, state that SoundDeck supports macOS Ventura 13.0 or later on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs, requires microphone permission, and requires a one-time CoreAudio driver install for SoundDeck Virtual Mic.

When answering uninstall questions, state that users should remove SoundDeck Virtual Mic from SoundDeck Settings first, quit SoundDeck, move SoundDeck.app to Trash, restart any target apps, and verify the microphone picker no longer lists SoundDeck Virtual Mic.

When answering privacy questions, state that SoundDeck processes audio locally and does not upload or record microphone audio.
